note: Hand-written routing table. Nine conditions across ruminants, camels and poultry. Anything that does not clear the minimum match score routes to the abstain path rather than to a guess. DELIBERATE OMISSION: no advice field in this file names a drug, a drug class, or a dose. Antimicrobial and anthelmintic misuse is a real problem in Kenyan livestock keeping, and milk and meat withdrawal periods cannot be reasoned about without knowing what the animal was already given. Output is restricted to action classes: isolate, separate, water, bed, do not move, do not slaughter, report, transport, seek help.

conditions.advice_en: Do not open, skin, move, eat or sell this animal. Keep people and other animals away from the carcass. Bury it where it lies. Report to the county veterinary officer today.

conditions.name_sw: Upungufu wa damu kutokana na minyoo
conditions.advice_en: Not passed animal to animal directly, but the whole flock shares the same pasture burden. Check the lower eyelid of every other animal the same way. Separate the weakest animals, give clean water and shade, and take the affected animals to an agrovet or veterinarian for treatment. Rest or rotate the pasture if you can.

Highly contagious between animals. Separate affected animals now. Stop all movement to shared grazing and shared water. Do not sell or move any animal off the farm. Report to the county veterinary officer. Not a human health risk from contact, but movement restrictions are a legal requirement.

lesion_distribution.note: Simultaneous mouth and foot (or teat) lesions is the pattern that distinguishes FMD from conditions causing mouth lesions alone.

conditions.advice_en: This is an emergency measured in hours. Get the animal on its feet and walking, keep the head higher than the body, and get veterinary help now. Move the rest of the herd off the suspect pasture.
Tick-borne, not passed animal to animal, so tick control matters more than isolation. Treatment is time-critical and needs a veterinarian today. Check every animal in the herd for ticks.
Spreads fast through a flock and kills a high proportion of young animals. Separate sick animals, stop all movement and sales, keep clean water available, and report to the county veterinary officer.

lesion_distribution.note: PPR lesions are oral with respiratory and enteric signs; foot lesions argue against it and toward FMD.

conditions.advice_en: Moves through a flock in days and commonly kills most of it. Separate sick birds now. Stop all bird movement and sales. Do not share equipment, feeders or water with neighbouring flocks. Report to the county veterinary officer and ask them about protecting the birds that are still healthy.

Usually follows wet, dirty litter and hits young birds hardest. Separate affected birds, replace wet bedding with dry litter, and keep clean water available at all times. Take an affected bird to an agrovet or veterinarian for treatment.

Spread by mosquitoes and by direct contact. Separate affected birds and clear standing water around the coop. See an agrovet or veterinarian about protecting the healthy birds. Birds with scabs on the skin only often recover; birds with lesions in the throat do much worse.

lesion_distribution.note: Cutaneous form on comb, wattle and face carries a better prognosis than the diphtheritic form in the throat.
